approach: Add a small named helper in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs that reports whether an accepted reading has a Behavior criterion asking for a failing run without the fix, and change the gate at line 804-809 to `p.plans(reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_fails_without_run(&reading))`. JobPlanConfig::plans(hard) keeps its signature and meaning (enabled, and mode all or "hard" flag), so `off` and `all` are unchanged and only `hard` mode plans more jobs. The helper lowercases the criterion text, turns non-alphanumerics into single spaces, and matches a word starting `fail` (fail, fails, failing, failed) together with an anchor phrase (`without the fix|change|mechanism|patch`, `without it`, `before the fix`, `on the base`, `fails without`), so singular and plural wordings match. Tests: core tests in run/tests.rs drive Athena::ask/go in hard mode with a scripted reader and count planner/critic calls and inspect the verifier prompt. For the CLI test to see a `fails-without-1` record, the existing core-private demo_seam must be reachable from athena-cli tests, so its `install`/`Guard` are compiled under `any(test, feature = "test-support")` and re-exported from run/mod.rs under `test-support` only; the production build is unchanged. The CLI test installs a `sh -c` mapper, so no real cargo runs. Docs, the PlanMode::Hard doc comment and the changelog state the new rule.

decisions.choice: Fix the gate in Athena::dispatch (run/mod.rs ~line 804) by OR-ing a reading-derived predicate with hard_reason; leave JobPlanConfig::plans(bool) untouched.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where dispatch decides `planned`: it asks only whether hard_reason is set, so an easy job whose accepted criteria ask for a failing run never gets a plan, a plan demonstration, or the fails-without record the verifier sees. `plans(hard)` already means 'this job counts as hard for planning'; the existing config tests (config.rs 855-857, 1175-1181) pass unchanged and the three modes keep their meaning.

rejected.option: Add a second bool parameter to JobPlanConfig::plans
rejected.why: Changes a public signature and the config tests that must pass unchanged; the extra input is a property of the reading, not of the config.

rejected.option: Have the reader set hard_reason for such jobs (change the reader prompt or schema)
rejected.why: hard_reason also escalates the producer model, so it would change cost and model choice; the reader prompt is out of scope.

rejected.option: Use the structured fails_without field of a plan or a new Criterion field
rejected.why: Plans do not exist before the gate runs, and adding a field to the reading's Criterion record is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Match on normalized text of Behavior criteria only: a `fail*` word plus an anchor phrase, as a small named function with a doc comment.
decisions.reason: Fixes the previous attempt's finding that plural wordings ('tests fail without the change') were missed, while Content criteria (checked by reading) and bare 'tests pass' stay unplanned. Normalizing punctuation and quotes makes the quoted form 'fails without the fix' match.

rejected.option: A regex crate dependency or a stem list
rejected.why: Needs no new dependency; the anchor-phrase list is short and a unit test pins the forms.
'the build never fails' or 'a failing check is reported' would plan easy jobs for no reason.

decisions.choice: Make criterion 3 checkable by exposing the demo seam to athena-cli tests under the `test-support` feature (re-export `install`/`Guard` from run/mod.rs), and install a `sh -c` mapper in the CLI test.
decisions.reason: Today `install` and `Guard` are `#[cfg(test)]` in checks.rs lines 130-146, and `demo_runs_here` (checks.rs 94-97) returns false in a test-support build without a seam, so a CLI test could never see a `fails-without-1` record. The core test `a_planned_job_without_a_demo_runner_records_no_demonstration` (tests.rs 3241) confirms no record without a seam. With the seam, the CLI test drives the production dispatch, revert copy and classification and only the program that runs is replaced.

rejected.option: Assert only the plan records and the 'Planned demonstrations' section in the CLI test
rejected.why: Does not meet criterion 3, which names the fails-without-1 record in the verifier prompt.

rejected.option: Run a real cargo test in the CLI test
rejected.why: Slow, and the code comment (checks.rs 91-93) says no test starts real cargo by accident.

decisions.choice: No change to athena.toml: `mode = "hard"` stays; config.rs gets only a doc-comment update on PlanMode::Hard and JobPlanConfig::plans.
decisions.reason: Governance files are out of scope; the Hard doc comment would otherwise say only a marked-hard job is planned, which is no longer exactly true. config.rs is a listed deliverable, and its tests are unchanged.

rejected.why: Leaves a doc comment that contradicts the gate.

Run cargo fmt, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p athena-core run::tests`, `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test job_plan`, and `cargo test --locked`; run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` too to confirm it is unaffected, and record only the results seen.

risks.risk: The text match is too narrow (misses a wording) or too wide (plans jobs needlessly).
risks.mitigation: Limit to Behavior criteria and require both a `fail*` word and an anchor phrase; the unit test pins positive and negative wordings. An over-match only costs one planning round, never a refusal.

risks.risk: Exposing the demo seam widens test-only code, which could leak into the shipped binary or cause a dead-code or unused-import clippy error in a build without `test`.
risks.mitigation: The re-export is under `feature = "test-support"` only, `demo_runs_here` still needs an installed mapper, and the shipped binary does not enable the feature (athena-cli enables it for dev/test only; verify the athena-cli Cargo.toml line 31 stays in the dev-dependencies section). The step asks the producer to run clippy with and without tests.

risks.risk: The thread-local seam is not seen if the CLI fixture runs dispatch on another thread.
risks.mitigation: The seam is thread-local and the fake driver runs in the test's thread (core tests rely on this at tests.rs 3096); the guard is held for the whole test, and the CLI test asserts the roles before the verifier prompt so a failure is clear.

risks.risk: More jobs now cost a planner and critic round, which raises per-job cost under `hard` mode.
risks.mitigation: The planned job's preflight reserve already covers planning; the existing cap test pins the stop-before-producer behavior, and the change is bounded to jobs whose criteria ask for the run.

risks.risk: A scripted reader whose criterion text differs from the CRITERION constant in base_script makes the producer or verifier output mismatch and the job fail for a reason unrelated to the gate.
risks.mitigation: Make the test wrapper rewrite the criterion text in the reader, producer criteria_check and verifier criteria together, modeled on run_planned_behavior (tests.rs 632-648).

Asserts planner and critic each called once, in the order Reader, Planner, Critic, Producer, Verifier, and the verifier prompt contains 'fails-without-1: not a check'.
